title: AiaFetcher::batch_fetch length mismatch silently truncates via zip
close_reason:
Half stale, half fixed here.

The zip the bead quotes is gone: absorb takes a 'requested' count and ignores results beyond it, so the over-returning direction was already handled. What was still live is the lossy direction the bead actually worried about -- too FEW results silently dropping URIs that stay in the tried set, so the chain can fail to build where a correct fetcher would have completed it, with nothing reported.

Any count mismatch now trips a debug_assert in absorb. Took the laxer of the two options the twin bead offered ('or use debug_assert for release-mode laxness') rather than the hard assert_eq it recommended: the condition is a bug in the consumer's own fetcher and it degrades gracefully, so panicking would take down path validation in production for a fault that does not require it, and a reachable panic inside certificate verification is a DoS vector of its own.

One thing neither bead noticed: too MANY results deserves flagging too, because the promise is INDEX alignment. A fetcher that has lost track of the count has lost track of which answer belongs to which URI, so the entries that do get absorbed may be answers to other URIs. Handling it safely is not the same as it being correct.

Tests pin both directions; the graceful release path is not covered because cargo test runs with debug assertions on, and the rustdoc says so rather than implying coverage that does not exist. Duplicate of PKIX-q9hv.14. Commit follows.
